served: nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze
results: 1. nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: see-saw nystagmus
2. adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): adduction paresis of the LEFT eye with dissociated abducting paresis of the right eye on rightward gaze - internuclear ophthalmoplegia
3. MRI brain with DWI: bilateral dorsomedial PONTINE and LEFT THALAMIC infarction
4. MRI sella and orbits: normal - no parasellar or suprasellar mass
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acute ischemic brainstem stroke causing bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia and see-saw nystagmus, due to bilateral dorsomedial pontine and left thalamic infarction (likely hypertensive small-vessel ischemia).

Alternative 1: Posterior-circulation large-vessel ischemia, such as basilar artery perforator infarction.

Alternative 2: Demyelinating brainstem disease, such as multiple sclerosis.

Alternative 3: Ocular myasthenia gravis.
